title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 17. Mercy to Devananda
html:
The Lord announces that He is going to Mathura; Nrisimhananda paves His road in his mind and foretells that He will turn back at Natyashala; at Vachaspati's house the Lord delivers the afflicted and instructs Devananda Pandita about the Bhagavata

Verse 1

एकदा भगवान्कृष्णो भक्तवर्गसमन्वितः।
प्रोवाच मथुरां यामि भवद्भिरनुमोदितः॥१॥

ekadā bhagavānkṛṣṇo bhaktavargasamanvitaḥ|
provāca mathurāṁ yāmi bhavadbhiranumoditaḥ||1||

ekada — once; bhagavan — Bhagavan; krishnah — Krishna; bhakta-varga-samanvitah — surrounded by His devotees; provacha — said; mathuram — to Mathura; yami — I go; bhavadbhih — by you; anumoditah — with the consent.

1One day Bhagavan Krishna, surrounded by His devotees, said, "With your consent I am going to Mathura."

Verse 2

ऊचुस्ते दुःखसन्तप्ता बद्धाञ्जलिमवस्थिताः।
कथं के त्यक्तुमिच्छन्ति पदं तेऽम्बुरुहेक्षण॥२॥

ūcuste duḥkhasantaptā baddhāñjalimavasthitāḥ|
kathaṁ ke tyaktumicchanti padaṁ te'mburuhekṣaṇa||2||

uchuh — said; te — they; duhkha-santaptah — burning with grief; baddha-anjalim — with joined palms; avasthitah — standing; katham — how; ke — who; tyaktum — to leave; icchanti — wish; padam — the feet; te — Your; amburuha-ikshana — O Lotus-eyed One.

2Burning with grief, they stood before Him with joined palms and said, "How could anyone wish to part from Your feet, O Lotus-eyed One?

Verse 3

यतस्त्वं तत्र तीर्थं चाखिलं वृन्दावनं मधु।
आसीन्मूर्तिधरं पार्श्वे तव सेवापरायणम्॥३॥

yatastvaṁ tatra tīrthaṁ cākhilaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ madhu|
āsīnmūrtidharaṁ pārśve tava sevāparāyaṇam||3||

yatah — where; tvam — You (are); tatra — there; tirtham — holy places; cha — and; akhilam — all; vrindavanam — Vrindavana; madhu — Madhu (Mathura); asit — have been; murti-dharam — in embodied form; parshve — at the side; tava — Your; seva-parayanam — intent on service.

3For wherever You are, there are all the holy places, there are Vrindavana and Madhu1 — in embodied form they stand at Your side, intent on serving You.

Verse 4

लीलासुखविनोदाय यास्यसि मथुरां प्रभो।
तथापि तान्समुद्धर्तुं त्रातुमर्हसि दुःखितान्॥४॥

līlāsukhavinodāya yāsyasi mathurāṁ prabho|
tathāpi tānsamuddhartuṁ trātumarhasi duḥkhitān||4||

lila-sukha-vinodaya — for the delight of Your pastimes; yasyasi — You will go; mathuram — to Mathura; prabho — O Lord; tatha api — even so; tan — those; samuddhartum — to uplift; tratum — to protect; arhasi — You should; duhkhitan — who grieve.

4For the delight of Your pastimes You will go to Mathura, O Lord — and yet You ought to uplift and protect those who grieve."

Verse 5

आयास्ये शीघ्रमेवेति तान्सान्त्वय्य दयानिधिः।
गच्छन्गङ्गादर्शनाय वाचस्पतिगृहं प्रति॥५॥

āyāsye śīghrameveti tānsāntvayya dayānidhiḥ|
gacchangaṅgādarśanāya vācaspatigṛhaṁ prati||5||

ayasye — I shall return; shighram — soon; eva — indeed; iti — thus (saying); tan — them; santvayya — consoling; daya-nidhih — the treasury of mercy; gacchan — going; ganga-darshanaya — to see the Ganga; vachaspati-griham prati — towards the house of Vachaspati.

5"I shall return soon": so the Treasury of mercy consoled them, and set off for the house of Vachaspati2 to see the Ganga.

Verse 6

नृसिंहानन्दस्तच्छ्रुत्वा मनसि परिचिन्तयन्।
जङ्घालान्दातुमारब्धः क्षेत्रान्मधुपुरावधि॥६॥

nṛsiṁhānandastacchrutvā manasi paricintayan|
jaṅghālāndātumārabdhaḥ kṣetrānmadhupurāvadhi||6||

nrisimha-anandah — Nrisimhananda; tat — this; shrutva — hearing; manasi — in his mind; parichintayan — meditating; janghalan — paths (stages of the road); datum — to lay; arabdhah — began; kshetrat — from Kshetra; madhupura-avadhi — as far as Madhupura.

6Hearing of this, Nrisimhananda3 sank into meditation and began in his mind to lay out a road4 from Kshetra all the way to Madhupura —

Verse 7

स्वर्णरौप्यप्रवालाद्यैर्मणिरत्नगणादिभिः।
सूक्ष्मसूक्ष्मचीनवस्त्रैर्निर्वृन्तैः पुष्पराजिभिः॥७॥

svarṇaraupyapravālādyairmaṇiratnagaṇādibhiḥ|
sūkṣmasūkṣmacīnavastrairnirvṛntaiḥ puṣparājibhiḥ||7||

svarna-raupya-pravala-adyaih — with gold, silver, coral and the like; mani-ratna-gana-adibhih — with heaps of gems and jewels; sukshma-sukshma-china-vastraih — with the finest Chinese silks; nirvrintaih — stalkless; pushpa-rajibhih — with rows of flowers.

7paving it with gold, silver, coral, and heaps of gems and jewels, spreading it with the finest Chinese silks and rows of stalkless flowers.

Verse 8

जलाशयेषु जलजैः पद्मनीलोत्पलादिभिः।
शोभितं रत्नघट्टैश्च हंसजैर्जलकुक्कुटैः॥८॥

jalāśayeṣu jalajaiḥ padmanīlotpalādibhiḥ|
śobhitaṁ ratnaghaṭṭaiśca haṁsajairjalakukkuṭaiḥ||8||

jala-ashayeshu — in the pools; jala-jaih — with water-flowers; padma-nila-utpala-adibhih — lotuses, blue water-lilies and the like; shobhitam — adorned; ratna-ghattaih — with jewelled bathing-steps; cha — and; hamsa-jaih — with cygnets; jala-kukkutaih — with water-fowl.

8That road was adorned with pools full of lotuses, blue water-lilies and other water-flowers, with jewelled steps down to the water, with cygnets and water-fowl.

Verse 9

एवं क्रमेण संनीय नाट्यस्थलमपि द्विजः।
आलेख्य वनलीलां तां स्मरन्कृष्णस्य विक्रमम्॥९॥

evaṁ krameṇa saṁnīya nāṭyasthalamapi dvijaḥ|
ālekhya vanalīlāṁ tāṁ smarankṛṣṇasya vikramam||9||

evam — thus; kramena — step by step; samniya — bringing (the road); natya-sthalam — to the dancing-place; api — even; dvijah — the brahmana; alekhya — depicting; vana-lilam — the forest pastimes; tam — those; smaran — remembering; krishnasya — Krishna's; vikramam — prowess.

9Thus, step by step, the brahmana brought the road as far as the dancing-place5, and there he depicted the forest pastimes, remembering the exploits of Krishna

Verse 10

प्रभोरपि स्वभक्तानां पक्षपातित्वमेव च।
सुखी भूत्वा हसन्नृत्यन्प्राह भक्तजनाग्रतः॥१०॥

prabhorapi svabhaktānāṁ pakṣapātitvameva ca|
sukhī bhūtvā hasannṛtyanprāha bhaktajanāgrataḥ||10||

prabhoh — the Lord's; api — also; sva-bhaktanam — for His devotees; pakshapatitvam — partiality; eva — indeed; cha — and; sukhi — happy; bhutva — becoming; hasan — laughing; nrityan — dancing; praha — said; bhakta-jana-agratah — before the devotees.

10and the Lord's partiality towards His devotees. And, happy, laughing and dancing, he said before the devotees:

Verse 11

अधुना न गमिष्यति मथुरां भगवान्प्रति।
आयास्यतीति जानन्तु कृष्णनाट्यस्थलादपि॥११॥

adhunā na gamiṣyati mathurāṁ bhagavānprati|
āyāsyatīti jānantu kṛṣṇanāṭyasthalādapi||11||

adhuna — now; na — not; gamishyati — will go; mathuram prati — to Mathura; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ayasyati — will return; iti — that; janantu — know (you all); krishna-natya-sthalat — from Krishna's dancing-place; api — even.

11"Bhagavan will not go to Mathura now — know that from Krishna's dancing-place He will come back."

Verse 12

श्रुत्वा भक्तगणाः सर्वे तद्वाक्यममृतं शुभम्।
पिबन्तस्तं परिक्रम्य दण्डवत्पतिता भुवि॥१२॥

śrutvā bhaktagaṇāḥ sarve tadvākyamamṛtaṁ śubham|
pibantastaṁ parikramya daṇḍavatpatitā bhuvi||12||

shrutva — hearing; bhakta-ganah — the devotees; sarve — all; tat-vakyam — his words; amritam — nectar; shubham — auspicious; pibantah — drinking; tam — him; parikramya — circling; danda-vat — like sticks; patitah — fell; bhuvi — to the ground.

12Hearing these auspicious words, all the devotees drank them in like nectar; then they walked around him and fell to the ground like sticks.

Verse 13

सोऽनमत्प्रेमपूर्णात्मा समालिङ्ग्य परस्परम्।
प्राप्तास्तद्दर्शनसुखं बभूवुरतिहर्षिताः॥१३॥

so'namatpremapūrṇātmā samāliṅgya parasparam|
prāptāstaddarśanasukhaṁ babhūvuratiharṣitāḥ||13||

sah — he; anamat — bowed; prema-purna-atma — his heart full of love; samalingya — embracing; parasparam — one another; praptah — having obtained; tat-darshana-sukham — the joy of seeing Him; babhuvuh — became; ati-harshitah — overjoyed.

13And he, his heart full of love, bowed to them in return; they all embraced one another and were overjoyed, as if they had already obtained the happiness of seeing the Lord.

Verse 14

ततो जगन्मङ्गलमच्युतः स्वयं
श्रीकृष्णसङ्कीर्तनमेव कृत्वा।
वाचस्पतेर्ब्राह्मणसत्तमस्य
गृहं समीयात्स्वजनैः परीतः॥१४॥

tato jaganmaṅgalamacyutaḥ svayaṁ
śrīkṛṣṇasaṅkīrtanameva kṛtvā|
vācaspaterbrāhmaṇasattamasya
gṛhaṁ samīyātsvajanaiḥ parītaḥ||14||

tatah — then; jagat-mangalam — bringing good to the world; achyutah — Achyuta; svayam — Himself; shri-krishna-sankirtanam — the sankirtana of Sri Krishna; eva — indeed; kritva — performing; vachaspateh — of Vachaspati; brahmana-sattamasya — the best of brahmanas; griham — to the house; samiyat — came; sva-janaih — by His own people; paritah — surrounded.

14Meanwhile Achyuta Himself, performing the sankirtana of Sri Krishna that brings good to the world, came, surrounded by His own people, to the house of Vachaspati, the best of brahmanas.

Verse 15

श्रीमन्नवद्वीपनिवासिनो ये-
ऽपरे जना ये सुरलोकवासिनः।
मूर्त्या सुदृष्ट्वा मुखपङ्कजं प्रभो-
र्वाञ्छन्ति ते नेत्रशतं हि सर्वतः॥१५॥

śrīmannavadvīpanivāsino ye-
'pare janā ye suralokavāsinaḥ|
mūrtyā sudṛṣṭvā mukhapaṅkajaṁ prabho-
rvāñchanti te netraśataṁ hi sarvataḥ||15||

shrimat-navadvipa-nivasinah — the dwellers of glorious Navadvipa; ye — who; apare — other; janah — people; ye — who; sura-loka-vasinah — dwellers of the world of the gods; murtya — in person; sudrishtva — having beheld; mukha-pankajam — the lotus face; prabhoh — of the Lord; vanchhanti — wish for; te — they; netra-shatam — a hundred eyes; hi — indeed; sarvatah — on every side.

15The dwellers of glorious Navadvipa, and other people — those who dwell in the world of the gods — having beheld in person the lotus face of the Lord, longed for a hundred eyes on every side.

Verse 16

दिनं कतिपयं कृष्ण उषित्वा द्विजमन्दिरे।
उद्दधार जनं सर्वं जडान्धबधिरादिकम्॥१६॥

dinaṁ katipayaṁ kṛṣṇa uṣitvā dvijamandire|
uddadhāra janaṁ sarvaṁ jaḍāndhabadhirādikam||16||

dinam katipayam — for some days; krishnah — Krishna; ushitva — staying; dvija-mandire — in the brahmana's house; uddadhara — delivered; janam — the people; sarvam — all; jada-andha-badhira-adikam — the dull, the blind, the deaf and others.

16Staying some days in the brahmana's house, Krishna delivered all the people — the dumb, the blind, the deaf and the rest.

Verse 17

वक्रेश्वरकृपापात्रो देवानन्दः सुपण्डितः।
आगत्य प्रभुपादे च निवेद्य पूर्वदुर्मतिम्॥१७॥

vakreśvarakṛpāpātro devānandaḥ supaṇḍitaḥ|
āgatya prabhupāde ca nivedya pūrvadurmatim||17||

vakreshvara-kripa-patrah — the recipient of Vakreshvara's mercy; devanandah — Devananda; su-panditah — the learned pandita; agatya — coming; prabhu-pade — to the Lord's feet; cha — and; nivedya — confessing; purva-durmatim — his former ill will.

17The learned Devananda Pandita6, who had received the mercy of Vakreshvara, came to the Lord's feet, confessed his former ill will,

Verse 18

पप्रच्छ निजहितं च तस्मै प्राह कृपानिधिः।
श्रीमद्भागवतं साक्षात्सच्चिदानन्दविग्रहम्॥१८॥

papraccha nijahitaṁ ca tasmai prāha kṛpānidhiḥ|
śrīmadbhāgavataṁ sākṣātsaccidānandavigraham||18||

papraccha — asked; nija-hitam — about his own good; cha — and; tasmai — to him; praha — said; kripa-nidhih — the treasury of mercy; shrimad-bhagavatam — the Srimad Bhagavatam; sakshat — directly; sat-chit-ananda-vigraham — the embodiment of being, consciousness and bliss.

18and asked what his true good might be. And the Treasury of mercy said to him: "Know that the Srimad Bhagavatam is Sri Krishna Himself, directly — the embodiment of being, consciousness and bliss,

Verse 19

श्रीकृष्णमेव जानीहि मात्सर्यादिविवर्जितम्।
पठन्भक्तिरसास्वादं प्राप्तानन्दो भविष्यति॥१९॥

śrīkṛṣṇameva jānīhi mātsaryādivivarjitam|
paṭhanbhaktirasāsvādaṁ prāptānando bhaviṣyati||19||

shri-krishnam — as Sri Krishna; eva — Himself; janihi — know; matsarya-adi-vivarjitam — free from envy and the like; pathan — one who reads; bhakti-rasa-asvadam — the taste of the rasa of devotion; prapta-anandah — one who has attained bliss; bhavishyati — will become.

19free from envy and every taint7. Whoever reads it, tasting the rasa of devotion, will attain bliss."

Verse 20

श्रुत्वा विप्रो नमन्मूर्ध्ना तत्पादरजसावृतः।
गौरचन्द्ररसे मग्नो ननर्त परमाद्भुतम्॥२०॥

śrutvā vipro namanmūrdhnā tatpādarajasāvṛtaḥ|
gauracandrarase magno nanarta paramādbhutam||20||

shrutva — hearing; viprah — the brahmana; naman — bowing; murdhna — with his head; tat-pada-rajasa-avritah — covered with the dust of His feet; gaurachandra-rase — in the rasa of Gaurachandra; magnah — immersed; nanarta — danced; parama-adbhutam — most wondrously.

20Hearing this, the brahmana bowed his head and, covered with the dust of His feet, immersed in the rasa of Gaurachandra, danced most wondrously.

Thus ends the seventeenth sarga, "Mercy to Devananda" (Devananda-anugraha), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Madhu (Madhupura, Madhupuri): Mathura.
  2. Vachaspati: a brahmana living by the Ganga in Bengal; according to other biographies, Vidya-Vachaspati, the brother of Sarvabhauma.
  3. Nrisimhananda: Pradyumna Brahmachari, a devotee of the Lord, so named for his worship of Nrisimha. The story is also told in the "Chaitanya Charitamrita" (Madhya 1).
  4. The word rendered here as "road" is obscure in the editions; the sense is clear from verses 7–9.
  5. The dancing-place: Kanai Natyashala, a village on the road to Vrindavana, from which the Lord turned back on that occasion.
  6. Devananda Pandita: a reciter of the Bhagavata in Navadvipa who had once offended Srivasa; he received the Lord's mercy through the intercession of Vakreshvara Pandita (told at length in Vrindavana Dasa's "Chaitanya Bhagavata").
  7. Cf. Bhagavata Purana 1.1.2: this book is for the righteous, who are free from envy.
